newsitem.title: USA: Poway, Calif., recovery plan backed by bondholders.
newsitem.headline: Poway, Calif., recovery plan backed by bondholders.

text.p: Bondholders have approved the terms of a workout plan that should prevent nearly $36 million of Poway, Calif., bonds from going into default in August, the city's investment banker said Friday.

Under the plan, a San Diego real estate developer, McMillin Cos, is required to complete $6.8 million in road and utility improvements in a partially completed industrial park and pay $5.2 million of the outstanding taxes on the property, investment banker Stone & Youngberg LLC said.
The city, in return, has agreed to contribute some redevelopment tax increment funds to the project.
William Huck, who heads Stone & Youngberg's workout team, said the recovery plan would make the property viable. "We are pleased that bondholders consented to this workout plan," Huck said.
The Poway recovery plan now returns to the city council for final approval. McMillin must then complete its land purchase by April 1 to meet the workout's terms.

Without the restructuring, Poway's Community Facilities District #88-1 would have defaulted on the Mello-Roos bonds on August 15, officials said. Bond reserves have been depleted from previous debt service payments.
Stone & Youngberg said city officials had tried but failed to sell the delinquent properties on four separate occasions in order to raise funds to replenish the bond reserves.
